title: Restriction-insertion comparison in both point-stalk cone coordinates
statement:
Fix the finite-field coefficient datum [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$. All schemes below have $\ell$ invertible and use compatible small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\widehat R_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$. Use $D^b_c(T,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], completed pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and point sections $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For a geometric point $v:s\to T$ and $M\in D^b_c(T,R)$ put $J_v(M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lv^*M)$. Stalks and their representatives $[U,u,a]$ mean [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For a strict tower $T_\bullet$ of complexes with transitions $t_n$, write $H(T_\bullet)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_T:\prod_nT_n\to\prod_nT_n)[-1]$, $s_T((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1})$, with degree-$i$ coordinates $(b,a)\in\prod_nT_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nT_n^i$ and differential $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_T)a,da)$.

Let $N\in D^b_c(s,R)$, $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(k)$, $\delta=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ and $q:Q\to N$ any flat-term K-flat representative. Put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\widehat R_s}(A_n)_s$, $\mathcal H_u=H(((Q_n)_u)_n)$, and $e_u:J_u(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_u$ as in [lem-trf-bounded-quotient-stalk-realization]. Use the identity unit to identify $J_{\mathrm{id}}(N)$ with $\operatorname{Fib}_sN=\Gamma(s,N)$. Write $c_{\delta,\mathrm{id},N}=\Gamma(s,\chi_{\mathrm{id},\delta,N}^{-1})$ for the specified comparison of [lem-trf-stalk-compositor-tower-realization], and $R_{\mathrm{id},\alpha,\bullet}$ for the germ tower map of [lem-trf-germ-reparametrization-derived-descent].

Let $\rho_{\delta,N}:\Gamma(s,N)\to\Gamma(s,\delta^{-1}N)$ be restriction along $\delta$ followed by inverse-image colimit insertion and sheafification. With the scalar action transported by the canonical coefficient isomorphism it is a natural $R$-linear isomorphism. Put
$$j_{\delta,N}=\Gamma(s,\kappa^\delta_N)\rho_{\delta,N},$$
where $\kappa^\delta$ is the specified chosen-resolution comparison [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]; it is invertible on this derived-complete domain by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization]. At finite level, restriction, insertion, scalar insertion and the finite stalk comparison send a section $a$ to $[s,\delta,a]$, using source lift $\mathrm{id}_s$ and target lift $\delta$.

The normalization of $e_{\mathrm{id}}$ is sections of the actual completion unit, followed by identity-stalk identifications. On $\Gamma(s,Q)$ its composite with $\Gamma(q)$ is the chain map $z\mapsto(0,([s,\mathrm{id},\bar z_n])_n)$, where $\bar z_n$ is the image of $z$ in $Q_n$. The specified inverse-image comparison, compositor realization and germ reparametrization have representatives on this one resolution satisfying the equality of entire chain maps
$$e_\delta c_{\delta,\mathrm{id},N}j_{\delta,N}\Gamma(q)(z)
=(0,([s,\delta,\bar z_n])_n)
=H(R_{\mathrm{id},\alpha,\bullet})e_{\mathrm{id}}\Gamma(q)(z).$$
The shifted coordinate is zero on both sides. This assertion is invariant under canonical resolution comparisons and natural for all derived morphisms of $N$. It asserts equality of the indicated chain representatives, not a claim that reductions detect arbitrary completed derived morphisms.

proof.text: Obtain a coherent compositor system from the compositor-tower theorem, and obtain section restriction and its ordinary derived descent from the restriction model.
Use germ-reparametrization descent to choose the normalized e_v and the strict identity-to-alpha tower isomorphism R, retaining its germ formula and all realization isomorphisms.

Apply the identity model to obtain the natural strict completion lift a_0, its two coordinates, and its identity representative formula. Pack these choices into the unchanged source-section data structure.

Apply the automorphism model to obtain the finite insertion formula, the source representative equation and invertibility, and the equality of entire strict lifts for all complexes. Combine its source equation with the identity representative equation to prove the original representatives clause.

Rewrite both source lifts by a_0 followed by the Roos image of R. Naturality of a_0 and R and functoriality of Roos prove chain naturality. The coherent source-unit equation cancels the inverse unit and compositor in c, so c is identity. Compose restriction with the natural inverse-image comparison to prove derived naturality, and assemble every field.

I checked Stacks sites.tex Tags 0F4F (line 8514, the germ rule (V,y,U,phi) to (U,v(phi)(y))) and 05V1 (8558), and the blueprint place thm-trf-l-function-euler-product, Local powers (b), at lines 56-60. This is a one-level split with no new nodes; the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and there is no SGA. Step 1: rho = sigma^delta (it allows any automorphism, completed coefficients, no boundedness). The arrow delta:(s,delta) to (s,id) is invertible with inverse delta^{-1}, so restriction along it is bijective, and it is natural under Gamma(q). Step 2: the completion-unit model gives u_N[q] = rho_D[v_Q]; with e_{id,n}(x) = [s,id,x] applied diagonally this yields (0,[s,id,z_n]). Step 3: the definition kappa = [theta~][G q]^{-1} cancels Gamma(Gq). It is literal for the chosen resolution and moves to any Q by the invariance in Step 7; the step could say this order explicitly (advisory, not a fault). Step 4: I checked it against pullback-stalk-coherence with t = delta, u = id, theta = (id,id), u' = id: the image is [V,id,a|delta], and the pointed arrow delta:(V,id) to (U,delta) gives [s,delta,a]. Step 5: t_n theta_{n+1} = theta_n by quotient-tensor-insertion, so (1-s)A = 0 and d(0,A z) = (0,A dz) (checked by hand). The compositor coordinate formula with f = delta, v = id then gives (0,[s,delta,z_n]). Step 6: R[s,id,a] = [s,delta,a] on both coordinates and R(0) = 0. Step 7: naturality covers e, the compositor, R with roofs and kappa; kappa is invertible because N is derived complete. Edge cases alpha = id, N = 0 and non-cocycle z are fine. No duplicate: the nearby nodes are Frobenius-specific or have no germ formula (lem-trf-point-sections-completion-cone, lem-trf-point-transport-resolution-cancellation, lem-weil-point-automorphism-derived-transport-inverse). The item's dependency closure does not contain the item, so there is no cycle. I accept the four declared tool_uses; quotient-tensor-insertion is already on the unit's route, so declaring it is superfluous. No changes were made.
